17:12 Local Time, 13:12 GMT, 18:42 IST: Umpires have decided that the light isn't good enough and that will be it for the day. What a remarkable fightback from Afghanistan in the final session. It was 20-year-old debutant Naseer Khan who led the way, plugging away tirelessly from one end and bowling as many as 34 overs today on a pitch that didn't offer much to the bowlers. The left-arm spinner took the first four wickets to fall before Ziaur Rahman produced a beauty at the fag end to get rid of Antum Naqvi. Zimbabwe will be kicking themselves for the way their batters have squandered the initiative. From 200/1, they slipped to 212/4, and then to 247/5 - most of those wickets coming because of reckless shots on a very flat pitch. Credit to Afghanistan though for the discipline shown by their bowlers, even when the wickets weren't coming. They picked up just one wicket in the first two sessions combined, before pouncing in the final session.

So much to look forward to as the match progresses. For starters, Taylor has batted beautifully and will resume his innings on 96 tomorrow morning. Then there's the second new ball waiting in the wings for Afghanistan who have finished Day 1 on a big high. Let's see how this develops. That's all for now, goodbye!

17:14 Local Time, 13:14 GMT, 18:44 IST: Stumps on Day 2 and Zimbabwe will be delighted with their efforts. They would've wanted more than the 339 they managed after starting the day on 250/5, but their bowlers have done an excellent job so far. Muzarabani and Masekesa the two standout performers for Zimbabwe on a pitch that is offering some more purchase now. Most of the wickets in this innings have fallen to some cracking deliveries, as opposed to the first innings where the Zimbabwe batters played attacking shots and got out. Afghanistan will be disappointed that they had so many batters getting starts but not kicking on. Three of them were dismissed in their 30s with the top score being 34 from Rahmanullah Zadran. They'll need someone to score a lot more than that to get anywhere close to the Zimbabwe total. That's all for now. Until tomorrow, it's goodbye!
